newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar falls as RBNZ quiet on comfort levels.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar falls as RBNZ quiet on comfort levels.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar fell in Wednesday morning trade as Reserve Bank governor Don Brash, appearing before parliament's Finance and Expenditure Committee (FEC), stayed silent on the appropriateness of the recent easing in monetary conditions.
The kiwi dollar was quoted at US$0.6770/77 compared with US$0.6780/95 just before the FEC meeting the data was released, while the Trade-Weighted Index slipped to 66.57 from 66.75.
The Reserve Bank's MCI index dropped to around 760, 65 basis points below the bank's desired level for the September quarter and beyond the bank's stated 50-point comfort band either side of 825.
"The market is disappointed there was no firm rhetoric from Brash defending his 50 point tolerance band," said a foreign exchange dealer.
"If he was going to be staunch on that, he probably would have come out and said he didn't want conditions to ease further from where there were already.
"Because the market has seen he hasn't said that, they will keep pushing it down until the bank bites," the dealer said.
Brash's comments to the FEC contained little new information for the markets in the wake of Friday's Monetary Policy Statement.
Brash agreed financial markets considered monetary conditions were tight and that the market would try to ease as much as the RBNZ would allow.
